clue.text: Skip overturned on your old grass

indicators.note: something overturned is flipped end over end, so the word for skip is read from its last letter back

blocks.note: to skip something is to leave it out
the archaic form of your

explanation.surface: Someone hops backwards across a lawn that once belonged to you.
explanation.walkthrough: TIMO, the reversal, comes first, then THY, giving TIMOTHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Timothy is a common meadow grass grown for hay and pasture.

clue.text: Turn up one's nose at bridge game for children with 3, repeatedly

blocks.note: 3-down is STICKS, and Poohsticks is the children's game of dropping twigs off a bridge, so the game minus its sticks is Pooh
the same word again

explanation.surface: A sniffy grown-up disdains the bridge game the children are playing with sticks.
explanation.walkthrough: Poohsticks, from the Winnie-the-Pooh stories, is played by dropping sticks off one side of a bridge and seeing whose emerges first on the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To pooh-pooh an idea is to dismiss it scornfully, which is to sneer or look down on it.

clue.text: See 9
When tailored, are two of these items required?

definitions.text: When tailored, are two of these items required?

indicators.note: tailored cloth is cut and reshaped, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether these made-to-measure items must be bought in pairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: shoes and boots come in pairs, two of them needed at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear means shoes, boots and the like, which are worn and bought as pairs.

clue.text: See 20
Do teach about part of an electrolytic  cell

indicators.note: about can mean turned around or here and there, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to give a chemistry lesson on electrolysis.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathode is the negative electrode of an electrolytic cell, where reduction takes place.

clue.text: Central American costa eats too much cheese

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: Costa Rica is a Central American country, and this is the word paired with costa
over the top, abbreviated

explanation.surface: A greedy Central American on the coast overindulges in cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Costa Rica is the Central American country, so 'Central American costa' asks for the word that follows costa in its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft white Italian whey cheese.

clue.text: Epitome of voracity, the sheep element

blocks.note: wolves are the classic image of greed; to wolf food is to gobble it
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A fable pitting the ravenous wolf against the ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfram is the older name for tungsten, the chemical element whose symbol W comes from it.

clue.text: Soldier on board game given credit on board - spiffing!

indicators.note: to be on board a ship is to be inside the letters that stand for a steamship

blocks.note: a Jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, a soldier serving on board ship
a team sport played on a field or on ice
buying on tick is buying on credit
SS, steamship, the vessel you are on board

explanation.surface: A marine on a ship plays a board game and gets credit, and it is all terribly splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: Jolly hockey sticks is a jokey British exclamation mocking hearty girls'-boarding-school enthusiasm; 'board' is used twice, first for the ship a marine serves on, then for the SS round the credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiffing is a dated British word for excellent, the gushing schoolgirl tone the phrase parodies.

clue.text: Architectural style acquired spasms, not trophies

indicators.note: not tells us to take away the following word from the one before it

blocks.note: to have acquired is to have got
hiccups are spasms of the diaphragm
cups are trophies

explanation.surface: A building style that won convulsions rather than prizes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' works as a minus sign here: the spasms word with the trophies word taken off its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Gothic is the medieval style of pointed arches, rib vaults and flying buttresses.

clue.text: Complete opposite of "left in", reversed

indicators.note: the two words found are swapped round so the second comes first

blocks.note: the opposite of left is right and the opposite of in is out, giving the phrase right out

explanation.surface: A puzzle about turning a phrase inside out to find its exact opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal here swaps the order of the two words, not the letters within them.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright means total or utter, as in an outright victory with nothing held back.

clue.text: Single item of 4, say? Hop it!

indicators.note: say means as spoken, so we want a word pronounced like the item but spelt differently

blocks.note: 4-down is FOOTWEAR, and one item of it is a shoe

explanation.surface: A question about one boot, then a curt order to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hop it' is British slang for go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoo is the exclamation used to drive away animals or people, a brusque command to leave.

clue.text: A meaty cut for Olympian team finishing second?

blocks.note: the medal an Olympian gets for finishing second
a side is a team; finishing second places it after the medal

explanation.surface: A runner-up Olympic squad is treated as a joint of beef.
explanation.walkthrough: Olympian ... finishing second gives SILVER, and team gives SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Silverside is a British cut of beef from the outer thigh, often salted for boiling.

clue.text: Toxic substance applied, perhaps, to oxygen and hydrogen compounds

definitions.text: Toxic substance applied, perhaps, to oxygen and hydrogen compounds

blocks.clueFragment: Toxic substance applied, perhaps, to oxygen and hydrogen compounds
blocks.note: surface reading: a poison is put on some chemicals
setter's reading: the poisonous element phosphorus is combined with oxygen and hydrogen, which is a verb for a chemical treatment

explanation.surface: A chemist doses some compounds with a poison.
explanation.walkthrough: Phosphorus is famously poisonous; combining it with other elements is a single verb ending in -ate.
explanation.definitionFit: To phosphorate is to combine or impregnate with phosphorus, a highly toxic element.

clue.text: One offers fine shots, providing hope for glamorous leader in tabloid

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the word is taken
in places the preceding pieces inside the newspaper that follows

blocks.note: to hope for something is to pray for it
the opening letter of glamorous
the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A paparazzo hoping a glamorous star will give good pictures for the gutter press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine shots' suggests photographs, but means a mist of fine droplets.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray gun ejects paint or liquid as a fine mist, firing tiny particles.

clue.text: Oscar winner with very brief acceptance speech grabbing award

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing and holding, so the speech holds the award inside it

blocks.note: the shortest speech of acceptance is one word of gratitude
the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A film star wins a prize and makes a mercifully short speech.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is the Order of Merit, an honour from the British monarch; the briefest acceptance speech is a single word of gratitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Hanks won Best Actor Oscars for Philadelphia and Forrest Gump.

clue.text: Acropolis in deltaic form

indicators.note: in a new form means reshaped, so the letters are recast into a different word

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hilltop fortress built in the shape of a river delta.
explanation.definitionFit: An acropolis is a fortified high point of an ancient Greek city, a stronghold or fortress.

clue.text: Smoker's aid should be missing round hospital

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word for missing wraps around the abbreviation

blocks.note: something gone astray is missing
H is the map and road-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A smoker's inhaler has gone astray somewhere in the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing' looks like part of the surface but is the outer word, and 'should be' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashtray is the dish a smoker uses for ash and cigarette ends.

clue.text: This mixed test 99 entered is well chronicled

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled
a number that has entered something has gone inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
an oral is a spoken examination
IC is 99 in Roman numerals, 100 less 1

explanation.surface: A garbled exam paper that somehow ended up well documented.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'This' is mixed; 'test' is a spoken exam, and 99 is written in Roman numerals before going inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical describes events attested in records of the past, documented rather than legendary.

clue.text: Boy fights ape, beaten at 1961 invasion site

indicators.note: something beaten is battered out of shape, so the letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy takes on an ape and loses the brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bay of Pigs in Cuba was where US-backed exiles made their failed landing in April 1961.

clue.text: Talk of one passing tongue over alcohol

indicators.note: talk of means as it is spoken, so a word with the same sound is wanted

blocks.note: someone who passes the tongue over something licks it

explanation.surface: A drinker running a tongue round the rim of a glass of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquor is strong alcoholic drink, especially spirits.

clue.text: Don't hit a girl

blocks.note: first meaning: to fail to strike the target
second meaning: a young unmarried woman, as in the title

explanation.surface: A firm warning against striking a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to fail to strike, and the noun is a polite term for a young woman.

clue.text: Bird keeps maiden name with reference to novel

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the bird's name encloses the next piece

blocks.note: a jay is a crow-family bird
née introduces a married woman's maiden name
re means concerning or with reference to

explanation.surface: A bird clings to a woman's maiden name in a citation about a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Née, French for born, introduces a married woman's maiden name.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Eyre is Charlotte Brontë's 1847 novel about a governess.

clue.text: A couple of pints put on the last stone

blocks.note: a quart is two pints
the final letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone downs two pints and then piles on the pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is also a British unit of weight, 14 pounds, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Quartz is a hard crystalline mineral, a common stone of silica.

clue.text: Complaint  brings fat back around belt ...

indicators.note: back means going in the opposite direction, so the word for fat is read right to left
around means surrounding, so the reversed word encloses the next piece

blocks.note: suet is hard animal fat
to tan someone is to belt or thrash them

explanation.surface: A grumble that a fat belly is spilling over a waist belt.
explanation.walkthrough: To tan someone's hide is to beat them, so belt is a verb here. The ellipsis leads into the next clue, whose answer names the same disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint can mean an illness, and tetanus is a bacterial disease causing muscle spasms.

clue.text: ...or hair on chin

definitions.note: the ellipsis carries over the definition Complaint from the previous clue: another name for the same disease

blocks.note: a lock is a tress of hair
the chin is part of the jaw

explanation.surface: Following on, a beard is offered as the alternative to a paunch.
explanation.walkthrough: LOCK goes on JAW. 'Or' links to the previous clue: the definition is that clue's Complaint, since this disease is another name for tetanus.
explanation.definitionFit: Lockjaw is the popular name for tetanus, from the clenched jaw muscles it causes.
